exposure: mode of delivery (caesarean section, vaginal delivery)
outcome: problems of breastfeeding (difficulty in initiation, improper latching, inadequate milk production)
successful establishment of breastfeeding on Day 3
cohort: 180 women (90 vaginal delivery, 90 caesarean section) who delivered term babies in a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Caesarean section delivery was associated with later and more difficult initiation of breastfeeding compared to vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was significantly associated with late initiation of breastfeeding (7.8% vs 75.6% in vaginal delivery) and increased difficulty in initiation (52.2% vs 22.2%), with women undergoing caesarean section also experiencing significantly more post-delivery pain, improper latching, and inadequate milk production.
cross-section timing: Observations were made within 1 hour of delivery for early initiation and on postnatal Day 3 for establishment and problems.
